root_idea.summary: The root denotes probing or feeling something by hand, and thus direct tactile contact.
root_idea.development: From physical contact, the lexical field extends to mutual contact, an effect reaching or afflicting someone, euphemistic sexual contact, and related expressions of nearness or immediate effect.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Form I verb is a principal Quranic form with distinct tactile, sexual, and afflictive usages.
The Form VI verb occurs in a Quranic reciprocal construction with a specifically sexual interpretation.
The noun مَسّ has Quranic uses for the onset of harm and for madness or diabolical possession.
مِسَاس occurs in the Quranic fixed expression لَا مِسَاسَ and is lexically distinct from the ordinary noun مَسّ.

senses.definition: To touch or feel by direct physical contact.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for tactile contact or perception by touch, including direct contact without an intervening object.

senses.definition: To have sexual intercourse, expressed euphemistically as touching.
senses.usage_conditions: A metonymic construction used especially in statements about intercourse before consummation or before a lawful sexual relationship has taken place.

senses.definition: To befall, afflict, or overtake someone with harm, hardship, illness, punishment, or other distress.
senses.usage_conditions: The object may be an individual or a group, and the subject may be distress, misfortune, punishment, illness, old age, or a comparable harmful effect.

senses.definition: To have sexual intercourse with one another, expressed as mutual touching.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic reciprocal construction refers to intercourse between the two parties, especially in the expiation sequence concerning the ẓihār declaration.

senses.definition: The first perceptible effect or onset of harm, pain, heat, or punishment.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for the initial sensation or impact of an affliction before it becomes fully established or overwhelming.

senses.definition: A touch or state of madness, insanity, or diabolical possession.
senses.usage_conditions: The expression presents madness or possession metaphorically as a touch, particularly a touch attributed to the devil or jinn.

senses.definition: In لَا مِسَاسَ: “no touching,” “do not touch me,” or “there shall be no mutual touching.”
senses.usage_conditions: A fixed Quranic expression with variant readings and closely related interpretations of prohibition, refusal of contact, or absence of mutual contact.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wet a body, as water wets the body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived physical-contact use in which the subject is water and the object is the body.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike or smite.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical extension from contact by the hand; the construction may specify the instrument, such as a whip.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To affect someone with madness, insanity, or diabolical possession.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression portrays the person as touched by jinn or a devil; this verb-level use is distinct from the Quranic noun sense of مَسّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a need to be pressing, difficult, or distressing in relation to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized phrase whose exact syntactic direction is inferred in the lexical source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the haps or effects of good or evil fortune to happen to or betide someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended use of مسّ for events or conditions reaching a person, whether favorable or unfavorable.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a relationship to be near to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative proximity construction based on the notion of contact or nearness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take or handle a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metaphorical use derived from touching or taking something with the hand.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to touch a thing or enable someone to touch it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV takes the person as the caused participant and the thing as what is touched.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wet or smear something with water, perfume, or another substance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for causing a body or body part to be wetted or coated, including smearing the face with perfume.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a complaint to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized idiomatic construction with شَكْوَى as the conveyed complaint.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For two bodies or parties to touch one another or be in contact.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the general reciprocal-contact meaning; the Quranic sexual construction is listed separately under the Quranic Form VI form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An impress or visible indication of a good condition in a person's livestock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the observable state or quality manifested in camels, sheep, or goats.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water reached or taken by the hands.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: One lexical analysis treats the word as describing water that hands can reach or take.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wholesome water, saliva, or another thing that relieves thirst promptly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description may emphasize water that removes thirst as soon as it is touched or consumed, and extends to saliva or anything with that effect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water variously described as intermediate between sweet and salt, sweet and clear, or saline, bitter, thick, and undrinkable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are variant lexicographic descriptions of the water term rather than a single resolved water-quality definition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Herbage having a fattening or beneficial effect on grazing animals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension to pasture that benefits animals feeding on it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bezoar stone or antidote against poison.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized technical usage, with the two explanations treated as equivalent in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pressing or difficult-to-accomplish need.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is used with حاجة and is synonymous with an urgent or important need.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A near relationship or close kinship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative proximity expression applied to kinship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person affected by madness, insanity, or diabolical possession.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial description of someone regarded as touched by a devil or other possessing force.

cautions: The Quranic Form VI occurrences are specifically interpreted as reciprocal sexual contact; its broader physical-contact meaning is listed separately as Classical Arabic.
لَا مِسَاسَ has variant readings and closely related interpretations involving prohibition of contact, refusal to be touched, or absence of mutual contact.
مَسُوس has several competing lexical descriptions for water; these variants are preserved rather than forced into one narrower definition.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The phrase مَسَّتْ إِلَيْهِ الحَاجَةُ is marked as an assumed tropical use, and the exact direction of the difficulty is left partly to inference; it is represented as a pressing-need construction with that uncertainty retained.
The water-quality explanations under مَسُوس differ among authorities and are represented as variant descriptions rather than resolved into a single semantic value.
